questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Different views on a future in virtual worlds
How to watch football matches on your phone
Why Facebook is losing so many of its users
How computer games are designed and made
questions.why: Neil says they'll hear two different opinions on the 'metaverse' and how it might shape the future.

questions.q: What is Sam's problem on Saturday mornings?
options: She can't find a football match to watch
Her friends never want to go to the park
When the weather's bad, she goes back to bed
She has to work instead of watching football
questions.why: She says when it's cold and rainy she looks out the window and goes straight back to bed.

questions.q: Why did the presenters decide to look at VR again?
options: Many listeners asked for another programme on it
Facebook said it would hire 10,000 VR workers
A new VR headset had just been sold in shops
Mark Zuckerberg had visited the BBC
questions.why: Sam says when Facebook announced it was hiring ten thousand workers for the metaverse, it was time for another look.

questions.q: What does Emma Ridderstad predict for ten years from now?
options: Most people will stop using mobile phones
Nobody will work in offices any more
VR will only be used for playing games
We'll do what we now do on phones in 3-D
questions.why: She says 'everything that you do on your phone today, you will do in 3-D' – shopping, meeting friends, working.

questions.q: What else does Emma say will be possible in the future?
options: Mixing digital objects into the real world
Travelling to other countries without flying
Replacing all shops with digital ones
Living without any physical objects
questions.why: She says you'll be able to integrate digital objects in your physical world, making it more 'phygital'.

questions.q: Why does Dr Nicola Millard call VR 'vomity reality'?
options: Because most VR games are about food
Because the pictures look very ugly
Wearing a headset makes her feel sick
Because VR is very expensive to buy
questions.why: She says she usually needs a bucket close by if she's got a headset on.

questions.q: What else worries Nicola Millard about VR?
options: It will make people forget their friends
It uses far too much electricity
It is not realistic enough to enjoy
Spending hours in big, heavy headsets
questions.why: She asks, 'do I want to spend vast amounts of time in those rather unwieldy headsets?'

questions.q: What is the difference between VR and AR, according to Sam?
options: VR uses phones, while AR always needs a helmet
VR replaces what you see; AR adds to it
AR is older and much cheaper than VR
AR only works indoors, and VR only outside
questions.why: Sam says virtual reality replaces what you hear and see, while augmented reality adds to it.
